title: Norm Comparison by Interpolation
statement: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $p,q,c\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<p<2<q$. If $\|f\|_q\le e^c\|f\|_2$, then $\|f\|_2\le \exp\!\left(\frac{cq(2-p)}{p(q-2)}\right)\|f\|_p$, where the power means use uniform expectation on the cube.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean function f on the n-dimensional cube
p, q, and c are real numbers
The q power mean of f is at most exp(c) times its L² norm
replaced: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$, $0<p<2<q$, and $c\in\bbr$, with $\|f\|_r=(\E|f|^r)^{1/r}$. If $\|f\|_q\le e^c\|f\|_2$, then $\|f\|_2\le\exp\!\left(\frac{cq(2-p)}{p(q-2)}\right)\|f\|_p$.
